THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 -3-  NC: 2023:KHC-D:10876  MFA No. 100962 of 2014  C/W MFA No. 23614 of 2013  JUDGMENT MFA No.100962/2014 is filed by the claimants challenging the judgment and award dated 19.04.2013 in MVC No.608/2009 by the learned Additional Senior Civil Judge and MACT-VI,
Jamakhandi, (for short, hereinafter referred to as 'the tribunal') for seeking enhancement of compensation whereas MFA No.23614/2013 is filed by the owner of the offending vehicle questioning the liability fixed on him.

2. Brief facts of the case are that the deceased on 17.12.2008 was pedestrian proceeding on the road near the land belonging to Yallappa Manavalli and at that time a tractor and trailer bearing registration No.KA-48/T-3225 and T-3226 came with high speed, in rash and negligent manner and dashed the deceased from back side.
Due to which, the claimants being parents of the deceased have filed the claim petition.

3. Heard the arguments from both sides and perused the records.
NC: 2023:KHC-D:10876 4.

The learned counsel for the owner of the tractor and trailer submitted that the deceased was not a pedestrian but was fallen from the tractor-trailer which is loaded with the sugar cane crop and it was not in a moving position.
Therefore, the death is not a motor vehicle accident.
Hence, the claim petition is not maintainable.
Therefore, prays to set aside the judgment and award passed by the Tribunal.
5. On the other hand, learned counsel for the claimant submitted that the deceased was pedestrian and hit by the tractor-trailer.
Therefore, the Tribunal has rightly considered the same and passed the judgment and award which needs no interference.
Further submitted that an order of pay and recovery is made since driver was not holding driving license.
Hence, prays for modification of the judgment and award of the tribunal.

Shri. Subhas S/O. Kallappa Meti vs Basappa S/O. Bhimappa Kulai on 19 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/13401895/
3 6.

It is the case of the claimant that the deceased was pedestrian and hit by the tractor trailer, but the case of the owner of the tractor-trailer that it is not a motor NC: 2023:KHC-D:10876 vehicle accident since the deceased while on the sugar cane load which is on the trailer, fell on the land and died.
Therefore, the place of accident is not a public place and the death of the deceased is not arising out of use of motor vehicle.

7. Considering this rival submission, it is the evidence of PW.1, who is father of the deceased, has deposed that the deceased was going to unload the sugar cane on tractor-trailer as a pedestrian hit by the tractor- trailer and thus the deceased died.

Ex.P.1-FIR, Ex.P.2- complaint and Ex.P.6 - charge sheet which prove that the deceased died in the road traffic accident as hit by the tractor when the deceased was pedestrian by the left side of the road.
Therefore, it is clearly proved from the above said documents and evidence that when the deceased was going on the left side of the road hit by the tractor and trailer.
Hence, the deceased died.

Even though PW.1 is not the eye-witness but he was informed about the accident and accordingly, he has lodged complaint before the NC:
2023:KHC-D:10876 police.

Upon statutory investigation, it is proved as discussed above that while the deceased was pedestrian on the left side of the road hit by the tractor-trailer from behind due to which, the deceased died.
In order to rebut this evidence, the respondents have not led evidence.
The owner of the tractor-trailer has not led evidence.
During the course of cross-examination nothing is revealed so as to disbelieve the claimant's case.
Therefore, it is proved that the deceased died in the motor vehicle accident while he was pedestrian on left side of the road and hit by the tractor-trailer.
For the contention raised by the owner of the tractor-trailer, there is no supportive evidence.
Also the owner has not led any evidence.
Hence, as discussed above, it is proved that the deceased died in the road traffic accident out of use of tractor-trailer.

REGARDING QUANTUM OF COMPENSATION:
8. The deceased was aged 16 and  years old boy.

Even though the deceased is to be considered as minor below the age of 18 years, but in village the boy or NC: 2023:KHC-D:10876 girl above the age of 15 years are working in some other capacity apart from going to school for earning livelihood to the family.
It is commonly seen in the villages.
Therefore, these facts and circumstances and context it cannot be said that deceased was not earning member in the family just because of his age.
It is proved from the evidence on record as above stated the deceased was going for coolie work for unloading sugar cane.
Therefore, just because the deceased was aged 16 and  years old cannot be said that he is non-earning member in the family.
The accident is of the year 2008.
Hence notional income is to be taken at Rs.4,250/- as recognized by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.

In view of the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in case of National Insurance Company Limited vs. Pranay Sethi and others, reported in (2017) 16 Supreme Court Cases 680, 40% of the income is to be added towards loss of future prospects in life.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: There are totally two legal heirs.
The claimants are parents of deceased.
The deceased was a bachelor, 50% of his income is deducted towards his NC: 2023:KHC-D:10876 personal and living expenses.
Considering the age of the deceased, the appropriate applicable multiplier is 18.
Therefore loss of dependency is re-
assessed and quantified at Rs.6,42,600/- (Rs.4,250 + 40% minus 50% x 12 x 18).

9. In view of the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Magma General Insurance Co.
Limited v. Nanu Ram & Others, reported in 2018 ACJ 2782 and in the case of Pranay Sethi supra,

10. Further, a compensation of Rs.15,000/- each is awarded under the head 'loss of estate' and 'funeral and transportation' respectively, along with 10% escalation.
Therefore under these heads Rs.33,000/- (Rs.15,000 x 2 + 10%) is awarded.

Thus, the claimants would be entitled for compensation under various heads as under:

Therefore, the claimants are entitled for compensation of Rs.7,63,600/- as against what has been awarded by the tribunal along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of filing of the petition till realization.
The insurance company is directed to deposit the enhanced compensation within eight weeks from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment.
In the present case, the insurance company has taken contention that the driver of the tractor-trailer was not having driving license.

The investigating officer has filed charge sheet against the driver of tractor-trailer for the offence under Sections 3 R/w Section 187 of the MV Act, which proves that the driver was not holding driving license.
For non-having of driving license of tractor-trailer such offence is foisted.
Therefore, the insurance company is able to establish its defence that the driver was not holding driving license.

However, as per Sub-section (2) of Section Shri. Subhas S/O. Kallappa Meti vs Basappa S/O. Bhimappa Kulai on 19 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/13401895/
5 149 of Motor Vehicle Act, when the Insurance Company established the fact that driver was not holding driving licence, then as per Sub-sections (1), (5), (7) of Section 149 of Motor Vehicle Act, the Insurance Company as if the judgment debtor shall satisfy the claim in respect of third parties at the first instance and then recover the same from owner of the offending tractor-trailer bearing registration No.KA-48/T-3225 and T-3226.

Thus,
an order of pay and recovery is made.
To this extent, the judgment and award passed by the Tribunal is modified.

14. The learned counsel for the insurance company places reliance on the division bench of this Court in the case of Adilakshmammama and others vs. Raju B. and others, reported in MANU/KA/0947/2023 wherein it is held that in the case of non-possession of driving license an order of pay and recovery cannot be made.

entities.text: Adilakshmammama and others vs. Raju B. and others, reported in MANU/KA/0947/2023
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the above cited judgment Sections 147 and 149 are not discussed.

Simply it is observed that where there is a clear breach of policy conditions, the owner is liable to pay (2018) 3 SCC 208 (2004) 3 SCC 297 2020 ACJ 2560 - 12 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:10876 compensation and simply confirmed the order of the Tribunal holding the owner is liable to pay compensation.
15. It is true that in case of breach of condition of policy, the insurance company is not liable to pay compensation, as its liability gets absolved for violation of conditions of policy.
However, the legislature in its wisdom to protect the rights of third party has made provision under Section 149 of the M.V. Act for pay and recovery.

As discussed above even though the insurance company can avoid its liability but as if judgment debtor shall satisfy the claim to third parties then recover the amount of compensation from the owner of the offending vehicle.

This is the spirit of Section 149 of the M.V.
Act, and its interpretation is made in the above cited judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court and in the full bench decision of this Court.
But in Adilakshmammama's case (supra) the provision is neither interpreted nor made any discussion/ observation regarding principle of law laid down in the decisions as above stated.
Therefore, just passing remarks - 13 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:10876 is made by the division that is not the ratio to be followed.
Therefore, with great respect, the judgment in the case of Adilakshmammama is not followed in the case.
